name: OrbitalSpace
tagline: The whole planet, live, on one globe
summary: A live 3D Earth that puts temperature for 260 cities, GDP per capita for 193 countries and every magnitude 4.5+ earthquake on one globe, with a page behind every dot.
description: A live 3D Earth with temperature for 260 cities, GDP per capita for 193 countries and every magnitude 4.5+ earthquake, built by Kshitij Bhatnagar.
spark: Live weather, national economics and earthquakes each sit on different sites, maps and tables. I wanted to see the whole planet at once and go from a glowing dot on a globe to the numbers behind it in a single click.
build: I built one three.js globe with three layers: Stratum for live temperature and air quality, Meridian for World Bank indicators, and Signal for USGS earthquakes and NASA natural events. A scroll story flies a day and night Earth along one continuous camera path, and every city, country and quake gets its own page, live on orbitalspace.in behind Cloudflare.
architecture: One shared globe engine drives three data layers
Daily snapshot rebuild + ISR, browser polls each source at its own cadence
Scroll camera on spline paths, one continuous flight with no seams
highlights: Open-Meteo, World Bank, USGS and NASA data
A page behind every city, country and quake
Scroll story on a textured day and night Earth

name: Astrolenz
tagline: Vedic kundli, compatibility & AI palm reading, done right
summary: A Vedic astrology toolkit on a real sidereal ephemeris: birth chart (kundli) with shadow readings, 36-guna compatibility matching, AI palm reading and an AI astrologer you can question about your own chart.
description: A Vedic astrology toolkit on a real sidereal ephemeris: kundli birth charts, 36-guna compatibility matching, AI palm reading and an AI astrologer.
spark: Every big astrology app I tried buried the actual calculations under generic horoscopes and dark-pattern subscriptions, and only ever told you what was great about your chart. I wanted the real maths: Lahiri ayanamsa, proper ephemeris, actual Ashtakoot scoring, plus an honest read on the blind spots, in one clean place.
build: I built a full Vedic toolkit: a sidereal birth chart on the Moshier ephemeris with plain-English decode and shadow cards, 36-guna Ashtakoot matching with dosha detection, Panchang, numerology, a Sade Sati timeline and a Knowledge Hub. An on-device TensorFlow.js scanner frames each palm before Gemini reads it, and an AI astrologer answers questions about any saved chart. Sign in, credits and Razorpay top-ups run on Firebase, live on astrolenz.com.
architecture: Real sidereal calculations: Moshier ephemeris + Lahiri ayanamsa
On-device hand scan, Gemini palm reading on Vertex AI
Server-side credit ledger in Firestore, Razorpay top-ups
highlights: AI palm reader and AI astrologer
Free horoscope, Panchang and Knowledge Hub

name: VideoNote
tagline: Paste any video, get notes you can actually study
summary: Paste a link from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and more, and get a timestamped transcript, a chapter timeline, study notes, flashcards, a quiz and an Ask chat that answers with cited timestamps.
description: Paste a YouTube, Instagram or TikTok link and get a timestamped transcript, chapters, study notes, flashcards, a quiz and chat with cited timestamps.
spark: I save a lot of videos to review later but kept losing the thread of what I actually learnt from them. Typing out notes manually felt like busywork, and there was no easy way to pull the content into Claude without re-watching or describing it by hand.
build: What started as a one-field transcriber grew into VideoNote. It uses YouTube captions when it can and otherwise transcribes the audio with Whisper large v3 turbo on Groq, then writes a chapter timeline, notes, flashcards and a quiz you can question. Google sign in, prepaid Pro passes through Razorpay and a Redis usage meter all run on one Python function, live on videonote.in behind Cloudflare.
architecture: Captions first, Whisper fallback, audio deleted after
One Python serverless function, Firebase Google sign in
Disclosed daily limits, no fake reference prices
highlights: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X and more

name: ContextBridge
tagline: Shared memory between AI chats
summary: Paste a ChatGPT share link and get a clean, portable page plus exports, or let your agents pull it through an MCP server, so conversation context moves between ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and coding agents.
description: Paste a ChatGPT share link and get a clean, portable page and exports, or pull it through an MCP server to move context between ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
spark: A work network blocked a ChatGPT share link I needed, and more generally my context was trapped inside one assistant. I could not cleanly carry a conversation into Claude or an agent.
build: I built a bridge that turns any ChatGPT share into a clean page plus Markdown, JSON and 'copy-for-agent' exports, then shipped an MCP server so Claude, Cursor and other agents can bridge links and search bridged chats by meaning with an in-process embedding model and no API key. It now lives on contextbridge.in behind Cloudflare.
architecture: The share link is the source, storage is optional
Translate-proxy fallback for blocked networks
MCP server with 5 tools for any MCP host
highlights: MCP server for Claude, Cursor and more

name: Hapnin
tagline: A belonging engine for people new to a city
summary: Curated events and activities discovery that helps newcomers feel at home, warmer and less cluttered than the big ticketing apps.
spark: When I moved cities and joined a 1,000-person newcomers' WhatsApp group, every genuine event drowned under housing, jobs and marketplace noise. I kept missing things I would have loved to attend.
build: So I built a curated, community-first discovery app: verified organisers, structured listings and a deliberately calm interface: an installable, SEO-first PWA on a Postgres backend, live behind Cloudflare on hapnin.city.
architecture: Curated + verified supply chosen over open chaos
SEO-first SSG pages with per-event schema.org data
PWA · Cloud Run · Cloud SQL Postgres · Firebase auth

name: MoneyMap
tagline: Watch $1,000 grow across every market, honestly
summary: An honest, gamified multi-asset money manager on real market data, real fees and real Indian taxes. It shows losses as clearly as gains.
spark: Every 'get rich' tool I saw quietly hid fees, taxes and the boring truth that most active trading loses to simply holding an index. I wanted to see the honest version with my own eyes.
build: I built a gamified money manager that runs $1,000 of paper money across stocks, crypto, bonds and ETFs with real fees and Indian taxes modelled on every trade, benchmarked against buy-and-hold, ticking 24/7 on Cloud Run.
architecture: Honest by design: real fees, real tax, real benchmark
Swappable Broker + DataSource seams (paper now, real later)
Stateful ticker on Cloud Run + Scheduler + GCS ledger
highlights: Never fakes returns, honest by design

name: Jetstream
tagline: A cinematic companion for the whole journey
summary: One app for the whole flight journey: book, then track on an immersive orthographic globe with live status, delay predictions and a lifetime travel passport.
spark: I loved one app for tracking flights and a different one for booking them, and hated bouncing between the two. No single product owned the whole journey end to end.
build: So I built one companion for the entire trip: search and book, then track on an immersive globe with live status and delay predictions, then keep a lifetime travel passport, all rendered as tile-free SVG with no API keys.
architecture: Single swappable DataSource adapter (mock → real)
Self-contained SVG globe, no map tiles or keys
IP-clean, original design system
highlights: Orthographic globe with live great-circle arcs
Calm 'book' world flows into cinematic 'track' world

name: Gaussian Visualizer
tagline: Move the mean, watch the defects appear
summary: An interactive normal distribution for process capability: drag the mean, the spread and the spec limits right on the curve and watch Pp, Ppk, PPM and yield update live.
description: An interactive normal distribution for process capability: drag the mean, spread and spec limits and watch Pp, Ppk, PPM and yield update live.
spark: Understanding process capability from static textbook curves never clicked for me. You could not feel how the numbers actually move as the process shifts.
build: I rebuilt it as its own small app: an SVG chart where the spec limits, the mean and the shoulder of the curve are draggable handles, live Pp, Ppk, PPM and yield with a plain-language verdict, and a hero where simulated parts fall into a histogram as the process drifts, so defects visibly land outside the limits. It is one static page with no dependencies, served on this domain.
architecture: One static HTML file, no build and no dependencies
Accurate tail maths, so the Six Sigma preset reads 3.4 PPM
Standalone Vercel app proxied to /gaussian-visualizer here
highlights: Drag the limits, mean and σ on the curve
Live Pp, Ppk, PPM and yield
Presets from a 20 mm bolt to Six Sigma

name: Habit Tracker
tagline: The system for self-improvement
summary: A habit tracker that turns daily routines into actionable insight with streaks, analytics and beautiful visualisations.
spark: I would start habits on motivation alone and lose them within weeks, because I could not actually see my progress or spot where I slipped.
build: I built a habit tracker that turns routines into data: streaks, analytics and clear visualisations with drag-and-drop planning, so consistency becomes something you can watch and defend.
architecture: React + Chart.js insight layer
Firebase Auth + Firestore sync across devices
Deployed behind Cloudflare on habittracker.in

name: Off the Bench
tagline: Level-matched tennis for Delhi NCR
summary: A marketing site for a Delhi-NCR tennis community targeting former competitive players. The hero is a physics-accurate bouncing felt ball that drifts right on load and scrolls to centre as the Google Form appears.
spark: Local tennis communities were all advertised with the same tired filler and clip-art. Nothing on screen actually felt like the sport, or spoke to players who had genuinely competed.
build: I built a standalone marketing site whose hero is a scroll-driven, procedurally textured three.js tennis ball (accurate seams, felt sheen, pointer parallax) that slides from right to centre as the community form fades in. Concrete copy, zero filler, mobile-first.
architecture: Scroll-driven three.js hero, lazy-imported for SSR safety
Procedural felt texture + accurate seam formula on canvas
Physics squash, pointer parallax, smoothstep scroll easing
highlights: Fluffy felt ball with accurate tennis seams

name: Therapy Practice
tagline: A warm home for a CBT practice
summary: A calm, editorial one-page site for a CBT therapist, where clients learn about her approach and book a session, signature 'thought record' hero included.
spark: My sister was starting her CBT practice, and every template site felt cold and clinical, or buried the one thing clients actually need: a way to book.
build: I built a warm, editorial one-pager with a signature CBT 'thought record' hero and inline booking, so clients understand her approach and book in a couple of taps.
architecture: Zero-build static site, deploys free
Accessible + SEO / OpenGraph ready
Booking auto-detects Calendly / Cal.com

name: Two Cents Daily
tagline: An AI run YouTube Shorts channel
summary: A zero cost pipeline that picks a personal finance topic, writes the script, narrates it, times word by word captions and renders a vertical Short, then uploads it to the Two Cents Daily channel.
description: A zero cost pipeline that writes, narrates, captions and renders personal finance Shorts, then uploads them to the Two Cents Daily YouTube channel.
spark: I wanted to test whether a faceless content channel could be run end to end by AI at zero cost, instead of paying for a stack of SaaS tools to do each step.
build: I built one Python script that runs the whole studio: a local model on Ollama picks the topic and writes a hook, analogy, stats and action script, edge-tts narrates it, faster-whisper times every word, free image search fills the frames, and the render adds word by word captions and a slow Ken Burns zoom before uploading through the YouTube API.
architecture: One script, topic to upload
Word level timestamps drive caption sync
Posting stays behind an explicit upload step
highlights: Local LLM scripts, free neural voice

name: Buskers
tagline: A new home for Jaipur's dance school since 1995
summary: A full rebuild of buskers.in for Buskers Dance Institute, replacing a 2018 WordPress theme with a fast static site built around three.js scroll scenes.
spark: The school's site was a 2018 WordPress theme run by outside developers. The goal was to own it end to end and make it feel as alive as a dance class.
build: I rebuilt it from scratch as a static site the school owns end to end: three.js scenes that move with the scroll, GSAP and Lenis motion, a Leaflet location map, and Cloudflare in front, staged for the domain cutover.
architecture: Static Vite build, no CMS to patch
Scroll scenes on GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis
Cloudflare in front, instant rollback to the old site

name: LinkedIn Newsroom
tagline: Breaking AI news to an approved post, from my phone
summary: A personal newsroom that watches AI labs and news sources, rates every story, drafts a LinkedIn post with a designed 4:5 card, and posts only after I tap Approve on my phone.
description: A personal newsroom that watches AI labs and news sources, rates each story and drafts a LinkedIn post with a 4:5 card, posting only after approval.
spark: Big AI launches move fast, and by the time I had read the news, written a post and made an image, the moment had passed. I wanted to be early without handing my LinkedIn over to a bot.
build: I built a pipeline on n8n that polls 57 sources every five minutes, has TypeSafe's Jev model rate each story against four typed questions, and has Claude Opus research and draft the post in my voice with a rendered 1080×1350 card. Each draft arrives as one phone notification with Approve, Edit on Mac and Reject, and only an Approve publishes it through the LinkedIn Posts API with companies tagged automatically.
architecture: Jev rating gate with Claude Haiku fallback, Claude Opus drafts, checker pass on every draft
Approval over ntfy, no inbound tunnel
Health check restarts n8n on its own if it jams or goes quiet
highlights: Stories rated 1 to 10, only 9 and 10 get their own post
Up to 6 drafts a day, nightly digest for the rest

name: First to Apply
tagline: New job postings screened, priced and on my phone within minutes
summary: A personal pipeline that polls 214 company career pages every three minutes, screens each new posting against my profile, estimates the pay, and pushes the best matches to my phone before most people have seen them.
description: A pipeline that polls 214 company career pages every three minutes, screens each new posting, estimates the pay and pushes the best matches to a phone.
spark: Job board alerts arrive a day late, and by then a good role already has hundreds of applicants. Company career pages publish the moment a job goes live, so I wanted to read them directly and only look at the roles worth my time.
build: An n8n workflow polls the ATS feeds behind 214 career pages. TypeSafe's Jev model screens every posting with seven typed questions, Claude prices the shortlist and writes a fit and a risk line, and fixed priority rules decide what reaches the tracker and my phone. Top roles ask for a referral first and hold the application for 48 hours.
architecture: Jev screen with typed questions, Claude pricing that degrades gracefully
Fixed P1, P2, P3 rules so the tracker never disagrees with itself
Every step writes its result, one lock per step, no silent failures
highlights: Every dropped job keeps its reason

name: Inbox Triage
tagline: Every email labelled, and my phone buzzes only for the few that need me
summary: A Gmail sorter that labels every email within a minute and only alerts me for clients, customers of my products, replies from companies and real people. Everything else waits for one briefing at 11:00.
spark: Important mail from clients and customers kept drowning between bank notices, newsletters and job alerts, and filters could not tell a person from a template.
build: Apps Script on Google picks up new mail every minute. Rules from a Sheet settle the certain cases, Jev classifies the rest against the label descriptions, and Claude on my Mac decides only what Jev is unsure about. Alerts go to my phone through ntfy with buttons that teach the sorter.
architecture: Cheapest certain check first: Sheet rules, then Jev, then Claude
A sleeping Mac never hides a human: unsure mail from people alerts after 30 minutes
Never archives, deletes or marks mail read
highlights: 93.1% right label on a 289 email test set
One morning briefing instead of constant pings

name: My Life
tagline: A gen-AI trained on my own life
summary: A private, local-first memory of my life: a spinnable 3D globe of everywhere I've been, built from wearable transcripts and photo metadata, with a chat that answers anything about my past.
description: A private, local-first memory of Kshitij Bhatnagar's life: a 3D globe of everywhere he has been, built from wearable transcripts and photo metadata.
spark: I realised my memory of where I had been and what I had felt was scattered across photos and a wearable, and quietly slipping away. I wanted to actually see and question my own life.
build: I built a private, local-first life graph: a spinnable 3D globe of every place I've been from photo GPS and wearable transcripts, plus a local RAG chat, 'a gen-AI of my life', that answers questions about my past with real memories and photos.
architecture: Local-first RAG on Ollama, zero cloud cost
DataSource seam for wearable + photo metadata
Photo metadata only (GPS/time), pixels never leave the Mac
highlights: 3D globe of every place I've been

name: Jarvis
tagline: A self-hosted personal AI COO
summary: A phone-first, self-hosted AI assistant with a custom particle-brain face, human voice, sandboxed file and network hands, and the ability to delegate hard tasks to a frontier model.
description: A phone-first, self-hosted AI assistant with a particle-brain face, a human voice, sandboxed file and network access, and delegation to a frontier model.
spark: I was doing the same operational glue-work over and over, and wanted a private assistant that could actually act on my behalf, not another chatbot that only talks.
build: I built a self-hosted AI COO with a bespoke particle-brain face, wake-word voice and neural TTS, and sandboxed 'hands' for files and my network, a mediator that delegates the hard jobs to a frontier model, always behind human-approval gates.
architecture: Mediator pattern: local brain delegates to Claude
Sandboxed, path-guarded tools
Human-in-the-loop on anything irreversible
highlights: Safety gates on money & irreversible actions

name: Voice Copilot
tagline: Drafts messages in your own voice
summary: A private assistant that learns my texting voice from my own chat exports and drafts openers and replies, with screenshot OCR input so I never retype.
spark: I text nothing like the generic, try-hard openers messaging apps seem to encourage, and retyping context from screenshots to get help was tedious.
build: I built a private assistant that learns my texting voice from my own chat exports and drafts messages that sound like me, with Apple Vision OCR so I can paste a screenshot instead of retyping. It is strictly draft-only. I always send myself.
architecture: Local model of my own voice
Apple Vision OCR input, no retyping
Draft-only, no scraping or auto-send

name: Event Check-in
tagline: Register a family, scan them in at the gate
summary: Event registration and QR check-in: attendees register themselves and their family and get a QR code, and staff unlock a PIN protected kiosk to scan guests in and watch live attendance.
description: Event registration and QR check-in: attendees register their family and get a QR code, and staff scan guests in at a PIN protected kiosk.
spark: It started as the registration and check-in portal for a company Family Day, which needed families registered ahead of time and checked in quickly at the gate.
build: I built the registration flow, a QR confirmation and a staff check-in kiosk with scanning, name search and live stats, then generalised it into a reusable platform where branding, event details and the staff PIN are all configuration.
architecture: Swappable backend: browser storage or Firebase
Camera QR scanning with jsQR
365 unit tests with Vitest
highlights: Scan or search to check in

name: FARsight
tagline: A zoning-compliance copilot for architects
summary: A pre-submission FAR and zoning checker for architects: pick the region, upload an IFC design, and get a pass/fail report with the cited clause and the change needed to comply.
description: A pre-submission FAR and zoning checker for architects: upload an IFC design and get a pass/fail report citing the clause and the change needed to comply.
spark: Architects I know waste days manually cross-checking designs against dense, non-machine-readable zoning PDFs, and still risk a rejection at submission.
build: I built the compliance core first: it parses an IFC model with IfcOpenShell, computes FAR and ground coverage, and checks them against cited, versioned rule packs for residential plots. Delhi's numbers are verified against the MPD-2021 table and Gurugram's against the Haryana Building Code 2017, with Noida marked provisional because its regulations only exist as scanned PDFs. Detecting the zone from a map pin is the next step.
architecture: IFC (ISO 16739) parsing via IfcOpenShell
Hand-curated, cited, versioned rule packs
Deterministic gap solver suggests the fix
highlights: A pre-check, not a legal authority

name: DevTo Growth
tagline: An engine for technical-writing reach
summary: A toolkit that drafts, illustrates and publishes developer articles to dev.to, tracking what's live and what's still a draft.
spark: I wanted my technical writing to actually compound reach, but publishing, illustrating and tracking articles by hand was slow and easy to drop.
build: I built a Python toolkit that drafts, renders cover images and diagrams, and publishes to dev.to through the API while tracking exactly what's live versus still a draft.
architecture: dev.to API publish pipeline
Programmatic cover / diagram rendering
Live-vs-draft state tracking

name: Dev Automations Kit
tagline: The small glue behind background dev agents
summary: A minimal, working starter kit for background developer automations: worktree isolation, idempotency, locking and notifications, written to accompany my dev.to post.
description: A minimal starter kit for background developer automations: worktree isolation, idempotency, locking and notifications, written for a dev.to post.
spark: Each background automation I wrote needed the same plumbing first: isolation, locking, notifications and a safe way to run twice.
build: I extracted the roughly 80 lines of shared glue into a small kit, with a read only standup drafter to start safely and a PR comment resolver that tries fixes in an isolated git worktree.
architecture: Isolated git worktrees per run
Idempotency and locking in one shared script
Read only workflow first, write workflows opt in

name: Hackerman
tagline: A hacker style control room for your own network
summary: A gamified, hacker themed control room for your own home network and devices, served by a zero dependency Node server behind a passcode.
spark: I wanted one playful place to see and manage what is on my own home network, instead of digging through router pages and system settings.
build: I built a small Node server with no dependencies and an installable PWA in front of it: a passcode gate, a playful terminal style dashboard of the devices on my own network, and a Keychain backed reveal for saved Wi-Fi passwords.
architecture: Zero dependency Node server
Binds to localhost only, passcode gate
Installable PWA front end
